section.title: org.osgi.service.dal.functions.data
section.para: Device Abstraction Layer Functions Data Package 1.0.

Bundles wishing to use this package must list the package in the Import-Package header of the bundle's manifest. This package has two types of users: the consumers that use the API in this package and the providers that implement the API in this package.
Example import for consumers using the API in this package:
{@code Import-Package: org.osgi.service.dal.functions.data; version="[1.0,2.0)"}
Example import for providers implementing the API in this package:
{@code Import-Package: org.osgi.service.dal.functions.data; version="[1.0,1.1)"}

listitem.para: KeypadData - Represents a keypad event data that is collected when a change with some key from the keypad has occurred.

section.title: public class AlarmData extends FunctionData
section.para: Function alarm data. It cares about the alarm type, severity, timestamp and additional metadata. It doesn't support unit. The alarm type is mapped to {@code FunctionData} value.

formalpara.title: See Also
formalpara.para: Alarm, FunctionData

section.title: public static final String FIELD_SEVERITY = "severity"
section.para: Represents the severity field name. The field value is available with {@link #getSeverity()}. The field type is {@code int}. The constant can be used as a key to {@link #AlarmData(Map)} .

section.title: public static final String FIELD_TYPE = "type"
section.para: Represents the type field name. The field value is available with {@link #getType()}. The field type is {@code int}. The constant can be used as a key to {@link #AlarmData(Map)}.

section.title: public static final int SEVERITY_CRITICAL = 3
section.para: The severity rating indicates that there a critical alarm. The severity priority is higher than {@link #SEVERITY_MINOR} and {@link #SEVERITY_MAJOR}.

section.title: public static final int SEVERITY_MAJOR = 2
section.para: The severity rating indicates that there is a major alarm. The severity priority is higher than {@link #SEVERITY_MINOR} and lower than {@link #SEVERITY_CRITICAL}.

section.title: public static final int SEVERITY_MINOR = 1
section.para: The severity rating indicates that there is a minor alarm. The severity priority is lower than {@link #SEVERITY_MAJOR} and {@link #SEVERITY_CRITICAL}.

section.title: public static final int SEVERITY_UNDEFINED = 0
section.para: The severity constant indicates that there is no severity rating for this alarm.

section.title: public static final int TYPE_ACCESS_CONTROL = 1
section.para: The alarm type indicates that there is access control issue. For example, the alarm can indicate that the door is unlocked.

section.title: public static final int TYPE_BURGLAR = 2
section.para: The alarm type indicates that there is a burglar notification. For example, the alarm can indicate that the glass is broken.

section.title: public static final int TYPE_COLD = 3
section.para: The alarm type indicates that temperature is too low.

section.title: public static final int TYPE_GAS_CO = 4
section.para: The alarm type indicates that carbon monoxide (CO) is detected.

section.title: public static final int TYPE_GAS_CO2 = 5
section.para: The alarm type indicates that carbon dioxide (CO2) is detected.

section.title: public static final int TYPE_HARDWARE_FAIL = 7
section.para: The alarm type indicates that there is hardware failure.

section.title: public static final int TYPE_HEAT = 6
section.para: The alarm type indicates that temperature is too high.

section.title: public static final int TYPE_POWER_FAIL = 8
section.para: The alarm type indicates a power cut.

section.title: public static final int TYPE_SMOKE = 9
section.para: The alarm type indicates that smoke is detected.

section.title: public static final int TYPE_SOFTWARE_FAIL = 10
section.para: The alarm type indicates that there is software failure.

section.title: public static final int TYPE_TAMPER = 11
section.para: The alarm type for a tamper indication.

section.title: public static final int TYPE_UNDEFINED = 0
section.para: The alarm type indicates that the type is not specified.

section.title: public static final int TYPE_WATER = 12
section.para: The alarm type indicates that a water leak is detected.

formalpara.para: Contains the new {@code AlarmData} instance field values.

For example, the maps can be: {"severity"=Integer(1)...}. That map will initialize the {@link #FIELD_SEVERITY} field with 1. If severity is missing, {@link #SEVERITY_UNDEFINED} is used.

{@link #FIELD_TYPE} - optional field. The value type must be {@code Integer}.

section.title: public class KeypadData extends FunctionData
section.para: Represents a keypad event data that is collected when a change with some key from the keypad has occurred.
The key pressed event is using {@link #TYPE_PRESSED} type, while the key released event is using {@link #TYPE_RELEASED} type.

formalpara.title: See Also
formalpara.para: Keypad, FunctionData

section.title: public static final String FIELD_KEY_CODE = "keyCode"
section.para: Represents the key code field name. The field value is available with {@link #getKeyCode()}. The field type is {@code int} . The constant can be used as a key to {@link #KeypadData(Map)}.

section.title: public static final String FIELD_KEY_NAME = "keyName"
section.para: Represents the key name field name. The field value is available with {@link #getKeyName()}. The field type is {@code String}. The constant can be used as a key to {@link #KeypadData(Map)}.

section.title: public static final String FIELD_SUB_TYPE = "subType"
section.para: Represents the event sub-type field name. The field value is available with {@link #getSubType()}. The field type is {@code int}. The constant can be used as a key to {@link #KeypadData(Map)}.

section.title: public static final String FIELD_TYPE = "type"
section.para: Represents the event type field name. The field value is available with {@link #getType()}. The field type is {@code int}. The constant can be used as a key to {@link #KeypadData(Map)}.

section.title: public static final int SUB_TYPE_PRESSED_DOUBLE = 3
section.para: Represents a keypad event sub-type for a double key pressed event. Usually, there are two press actions and the key is not held down after the second press. This sub-type is used with {@link #TYPE_PRESSED} type.

section.title: public static final int SUB_TYPE_PRESSED_DOUBLE_LONG = 4
section.para: Represents a keypad event sub-type for a double long key pressed event. Usually, there are two press actions and the key is held down after the second press. This sub-type is used with {@link #TYPE_PRESSED} type.

section.title: public static final int SUB_TYPE_PRESSED_LONG = 2
section.para: Represents a keypad event sub-type for a long key pressed event. Usually, there is a single press and the key is held down. This sub-type is used with {@link #TYPE_PRESSED} type.

section.title: public static final int SUB_TYPE_PRESSED_NORMAL = 1
section.para: Represents a keypad event sub-type for a normal key pressed event. Usually, there is a single press and the key is not held down. This sub-type is used with {@link #TYPE_PRESSED} type.

section.title: public static final int TYPE_PRESSED = 0
section.para: Represents a keypad event type for a key pressed event.

section.title: public static final int TYPE_RELEASED = 1
section.para: Represents a keypad event type for a key released event.

For example, the maps can be: {"type"=Integer(1)...}. That map will initialize the {@link #FIELD_TYPE} field with 1.
